extracted.intended_audience: creative writers (poets, fiction writers, creative nonfiction writers) and small-press submitters seeking publication or contests
extracted.subtask_short: submitting creative writing to literary magazines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation preferences for submitting poetry, short fiction, creative nonfiction, chapbooks, flash, and visual art to literary magazines, presses, and contests; includes length/format limits, themes, submission methods, fees, and editorial taste notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction-only genre restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a fiction-only challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the April Fiction Potluck is explicitly limited to fiction; non-fiction or poetry entries will be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story word limit — under 5,000 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Send your best story in under 5,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given for the Fiction Potluck Challenge — strict upper word-count ceiling for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original work required
rubrics_metrics.description: Unwoven Literary & Arts Magazine is committed to publishing original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must not be previously published; editors emphasize originality and a wide aesthetic range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic range — traditional to experimental
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re looking for authors with an awareness that represents a wide aesthetic range, from the traditional to the experimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors explicitly welcome diverse styles — both conventional and formally experimental approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in language/images that move readers
rubrics_metrics.description: We look for language and stories and images that move us out of ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission evaluation favors work that evokes emotional or imaginative displacement — material that feels transportive or affecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept multiple formats (fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, visual art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open for submissions of short fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and visual art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several presses accept a range of genres and media; check each publisher for which combinations they accept for a given issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme adherence for themed issues/anthologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls specify a theme (e.g., Body Snatchers, Pride Out Loud, Time, Music, Night); submissions should address the stated theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors sometimes offer advice on how they interpret themes (e.g., Time may influence setting and character). Tailor work to the theme while following any provided notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapbook page-count — CantoMundo (15–25 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets are invited to submit 15–25 pages for the CantoMundo Chapbook Prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact page-range requirements when submitting chapbook-length manuscripts to this prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapbook page-count — Violet Winding Stars Press (20–35 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript should be at least 20 pages and no more than 35 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stick to the stated minimum and maximum page counts; submissions outside this range may be disqualified or returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapbook page-count — Black River Chapbook Competition (16–36 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contest for an unpublished chapbook of poems or prose between 16–36 pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include both page-range and unpublished status; ensure your chapbook meets both criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapbook page-count — Passionfruit (25–40 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines list length: 25-40 pages (slightly longer or shorter will be considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some presses allow slight flexibility but prefer manuscripts within the stated range; check if exceptions are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flash/short-short word limits (e.g., under 1000 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash Takes Flight contest requests fiction and creative nonfiction under 1000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flash contests frequently enforce strict upper-word limits; verify whether title counts toward the total with each call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poem line-limit (≤15 lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept poems of fifteen or fewer lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This publisher aims to publish works that are powerful in brevity; poets should note any additional platform-specific notes (e.g., form preference or submission method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-length manuscript submissions (open reading periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overheard is seeking full-length manuscript submissions (fiction, short story & essay collections, poetry collections, creative nonfiction) during an open window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presses may open limited windows for full-length book/collection submissions rather than rolling or per-issue submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative, hybrid, and multi-genre chapbooks accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Lost Kite Editions Chapbook Prize allows collaborative, hybrid, and multi-genre submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some presses explicitly welcome cross-genre and collaborative forms; check eligibility details for prize entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform requirement (Submittable)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be made via our Submittable page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several publishers require a specific platform (Submittable); submit through the requested portal to avoid disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform requirement (Google form)
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions through our Google form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some small presses use Google forms; follow the stated method and provide the requested fields/attachments exactly as asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished-work expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: We are seeking 1–3 polished poems and/or art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors use the word 'polished' to indicate they expect submission-ready work rather than drafts; revise and proof before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiny-form constraint — 10 words or less including the title
rubrics_metrics.description: 10 words or less including the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro/micronarrative contests may count title toward the word limit; obey this rule exactly for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary prize and award details
rubrics_metrics.description: Example prize: $50 USD to the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest calls will state the prize; confirm currency, payment method, and any additional publication or rights terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading/submission fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading fee: £5 (example for Passionfruit Chapbook Submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some contests and presses charge a reading fee; check refund/waiver policies and include payment as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission components — sample pages and cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: What to submit: a 10-page sample (.doc or .docx preferred) and a cover letter including a [requested detail].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many chapbook/book submissions request a sample and a cover letter with specific information (bio, publication history, or project description); follow format and file-type instructions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished material requirement for certain contests
rubrics_metrics.description: Contest for an unpublished chapbook (Black River Chapbook Competition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some contests/prizes require the submitted manuscript to be unpublished — verify what counts as 'published' and whether posting to a personal website or blog affects eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept all styles/genres (editorial openness)
rubrics_metrics.description: All styles/genres welcome: realism, fantasy, SF, speculative, …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where calls state 'all styles/genres welcome,' they are signaling openness to a wide range of subject matter and modes; still observe any length/format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting guidance (font/length per-submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example guidance: less than 5 pages (12 font Times…).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some calls specify formatting (font, page limits). Follow any specified font size/type and page limits; if guidance is truncated in a listing, check the publisher’s own guidelines for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline and decision timeline expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each call lists an expiry/deadline and sometimes decision/publication windows (e.g., decisions by July, publication expected in August).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit before the listed deadline and note approximate decision/publication dates; some calls run seasonal or rolling windows and may announce decisions months after the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual art acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals accept visual art alongside written work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting art, follow image specs and file-type instructions on the publisher’s site; check whether art submissions are judged alongside or separately from written work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor taste descriptors — 'craft-forward', 'whimsy', 'queer joy'
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors list specific tastes: e.g., 'craft-forward whimsy' and 'we’re looking for queer joy and gay wonders.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These descriptors indicate aesthetic preferences and signal what will particularly attract editors — tailor submissions when appropriate to align with expressed tone or sensibility.
